primary_diagnosis_treated: Diabetic nephropathy (CKD stage 2) with hypertension, microalbuminuria, and metabolic syndrome
nice_guideline_used: NICE NG203 (Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management) and NICE TA775 (SGLT2 inhibitors for CKD)

medications.dose: 2.5 mg orally once daily; titrate up to 10 mg daily as tolerated
medications.purpose: Reduce proteinuria and control blood pressure; slows CKD progression
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends ACE‑I/ARB for CKD with ACR ≥ 30 mg/mmol or hypertension; monitor creatinine & K⁺ after 1‑2 weeks

medications.purpose: Renoprotective effect and cardiovascular risk reduction in CKD
medications.nice_justification: TA775 (and NG203) advise dapagliflozin 10 mg daily for CKD with ACR ≥ 2.6 mg/mmol or eGFR 20‑45 mL/min/1.73 m², even without diabetes

medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction; CKD is a risk equivalent
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends statin therapy for all CKD patients for CV risk reduction

medications.dose: 0.5 mg orally once daily for 3 days, then increase to 1 mg twice daily; continue for 12 weeks
medications.purpose: Aid smoking cessation to improve renal and cardiovascular outcomes
medications.nice_justification: NICE smoking‑cessation guideline (NG209) recommends varenicline as first‑line pharmacotherapy

contraindications.reason: Accelerates CKD progression and promotes fluid retention; patient has CKD stage 2
Increased risk of hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury; NG203 advises against dual RAAS blockade
contraindications.alternative: Use either ACE‑I or ARB, not both

contraindications.reason: Risk of lactic acidosis when renal function is severely reduced; eGFR not available
contraindications.alternative: Defer initiation until eGFR confirmed ≥ 30 mL/min/1.73 m²

contraindications.reason: Dapagliflozin is not recommended below eGFR 20; patient eGFR unknown

assumptions_warnings: eGFR not provided – assumed CKD stage 2 (eGFR 60‑89 mL/min/1.73 m²) for dosing; formal eGFR calculation required before initiating ACE‑I, ARB, or SGLT2‑I.
Baseline serum potassium not available – should be measured before and 1‑2 weeks after starting Ramipril.
Liver function tests not provided – obtain ALT/AST before starting atorvastatin.
Allergy history not documented – verify no ACE‑I or statin hypersensitivity.
Serum creatinine 2.1 mg/dL is high for stage 2 CKD; confirm renal function and consider nephrology review if eGFR < 60.
treatment_summary: Start ramipril 2.5 mg daily (titrate to 10 mg) and dapagliflozin 10 mg daily for renoprotection, add atorvastatin 20 mg daily for cardiovascular risk, and provide a 12‑week varenicline course with behavioural support for smoking cessation. Monitor renal function, electrolytes, and liver enzymes after initiation and at regular intervals. Avoid chronic NSAIDs and dual ACE‑I/ARB therapy. Confirm eGFR, potassium, and LFTs before commencing and adjust as needed.
